patients.summary: Teacher in her late twenties with a BRCA2 mutation and a childhood Wilms tumor treated with left nephrectomy and abdominopelvic radiation, followed with high-risk breast MRI. Crohn disease is found by GI in early 2025 and controlled on adalimumab; in August 2026, after her last practice visit, a breast surgeon sees her for a left breast mass with biopsy pending.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
26 y/o woman, elementary school teacher, new to me. Feels well, no complaints, came mostly so someone is minding her cancer-risk screening.

Oncologic hx: Wilms tumor, stage II, at age 6 -> L nephrectomy plus abdominal/pelvic radiation at a children's hospital. Off surveillance for years, no recurrence. She does not have the treatment summary but thinks no further follow-up was set up after age 18. Single kidney.
Genetics: BRCA2 pathogenic variant, tested ~2017 after mom's diagnosis. Has had breast MRI yearly; last one last year at her old office, she says normal. Not yet discussed ovarian risk management in any detail.
FHx: mother breast ca at 45 (living). Maternal aunt ovarian ca at 52. Maternal grandmother breast ca at 68. Has an older sister.
PSH: L nephrectomy (age 6). Radiation as above.
Meds: vitamin D3 2000 units daily, OTC.
Allergies: none to drugs.
Social: never smoked. Wine once or twice a month. Lives in Belchertown, walks and runs most days, eats a lot of produce.
Gyn: regular cycles, Pap last year at prior office, she believes normal.
Imm: thinks she is up to date, had both COVID shots this spring; records coming.

ROS negative x 12 systems.

Exam: NAD. HEENT clear. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement or nodes. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, healed L flank/transverse scar, nontender, no masses or organomegaly. Breasts: deferred today, she prefers to defer, gets imaging. Skin no rashes. Ext no edema. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P
1. BRCA2 carrier - continue annual breast MRI; order placed for November so it lines up with her prior cycle. Mammography to start at 30. Will revisit ovarian planning in a few years, she is not ready to talk about it now.
2. Hx Wilms tumor s/p L nephrectomy and abdominopelvic RT - solitary kidney: yearly creatinine and UA, avoid NSAIDs regularly. Will look up the long-term follow-up guidance for childhood radiation once old records arrive.
3. Health maintenance - CBC, CMP, lipids, UA, HIV and hep C screen today. Flu shot in October. PHQ-2 0.
4. Vitamin D - continue her supplement.
Release signed, request faxed to prior PCP. RTC 1 yr.

orders.reason: colorectal cancer screening plan after childhood abdominopelvic radiation

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Erin, 28. Here for yearly exam. Feels great. No abdominal pain, normal bowel habits, no bleeding, no weight change. No breast lumps.

She read a survivorship article over spring break and asked whether her childhood radiation changes what she needs for colon screening. It does: survivors who had abdominal or pelvic radiation are generally advised to start colonoscopy much earlier than the general population, often around 30. I don't want to guess the interval on my own, so GI referral placed to set a plan.

Meds: D3. NKDA. SH unchanged, no tobacco, wine rarely.

Exam: Well. BP fine. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses, no hepatosplenomegaly. Breast exam normal bilaterally. No lymphadenopathy. Skin normal.

A/P
1. Hx Wilms tumor with abdominopelvic RT - GI referral for screening plan.
2. BRCA2 - MRI 11/2023 negative. Next 11/2024. Mammography starts next year at 30.
3. Solitary kidney - labs today.
4. Health maintenance - Pap 2023 normal; vaccines in fall. PHQ-2 0.
RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Lab Results and Referral
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your labs were all normal. Kidney function unchanged. GI should call you within a couple of weeks to schedule; let us know if you haven't heard by mid-May.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY GROUP - CONSULTATION
Date of service: 06/10/2024
Referring: primary care
Reason: screening recommendations given childhood cancer treatment history

Thank you for asking us to see Ms. Winslow, a 29-year-old teacher. She comes in feeling well, with no GI complaints at all, wanting to know which extra cancer screening her history calls for. Her vaccinations are current per her report.

History: stage II Wilms tumor at 6, managed by left nephrectomy followed by radiation to the abdomen and pelvis; no recurrence since. Known BRCA2 mutation carrier, followed with annual breast MRI through primary care.
Medications: cholecalciferol 2000 units daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: mother with breast cancer diagnosed at 45.
Social: no tobacco, alcohol rare. Eats a produce-heavy diet and exercises on a regular basis.

Exam: vitals normal. Abdomen soft, nontender, nondistended, no mass, no organomegaly; healed left flank incision.

Impression: History of childhood Wilms tumor with abdominopelvic radiation therapy, which places her at increased risk for a second colorectal cancer.

Recommendations:
1. Begin screening colonoscopy at age 30 (spring 2025), then every 5 years if normal. Our office will contact her next spring to schedule.
2. No colon testing needed before then while asymptomatic.
3. Breast and gynecologic risk management per PCP and her established screening.

Thank you for this referral.

documents.title: Outside Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: GI consult letter from 6/10 finally received (requested twice). Matches what she told us in June. Colonoscopy at 30, q5y. Problem list updated.

documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just wanted to let you know I saw the GI doctor Monday. She said because of the radiation I should start colonoscopies at 30 and then every 5 years, so next spring. Nothing needed before that. She said she'd send you a letter.

documents.title: Re: GI Appointment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the update, that's the plan I expected. I'll watch for the letter and note the colonoscopy for next year.

Amount of fibroglandular tissue: heterogeneous. Background parenchymal enhancement: minimal. No enhancing mass, non-mass enhancement or suspicious focus in either breast. No skin thickening. Axillary nodes normal.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of malignancy. BI-RADS 1, negative. Continue annual MRI; begin annual mammography at age 30.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your MRI was negative again. Next spring we'll add a mammogram once you turn 30, and GI will be in touch about the colonoscopy.

orders.reason: two months of diarrhea, fevers and weight loss; please see soon

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Since around early-mid November, loose stools on and off, some days 4-5, some days formed. Tired, which she first blamed on report cards and the holidays. Evenings she sometimes feels warm, has seen 99s on her thermometer. Weight is down; she noticed clothes looser and our scale agrees (63 kg last spring). No blood that she has seen. No travel, no antibiotics this year, nobody at home sick. No joint pain, rash or eye symptoms. No urinary symptoms.
Meds: D3. NKDA.

O: Vitals as charted. Looks tired but not ill. Mucous membranes moist. Abdomen soft, mildly tender diffusely without guarding, active bowel sounds, no mass. Old L flank scar.

A/P: 2 months of intermittent diarrhea with low-grade fever and weight loss in a 29 y/o. Infection less likely at this duration but will send stool culture. Inflammatory bowel disease is the main concern. Radiation-related bowel injury and, given her history, a neoplasm also need to be excluded, and she already has a GI relationship.
- CBC w diff, CMP today; stool culture kit given.
- GI referral, urgent; I also called the GI office and asked for an earlier slot than the spring colonoscopy plan.
- Fluids, no NSAIDs (single kidney anyway).
- Call or message if blood in stool, fever over 101, or worse pain.

documents.title: Test Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Erin, blood counts, kidney and liver tests are normal, and the stool culture did not grow any infection. GI has you on 2/10, which is the earliest they had. If things get worse before then, tell me and I'll push.

documents.title: Re: Test Results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Ok thank you. Same as last week, not worse. I'll keep the 10th.

documents.title: Blood in Stool
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Sorry to bother you so early. Last night there was bright red blood mixed in once when I went. Hasn't happened again this morning. No dizziness. Should I go somewhere?

documents.title: Re: Blood in Stool
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Not a bother. One episode without dizziness doesn't need the ER. If it happens repeatedly, if you feel lightheaded, or the pain picks up, go to the emergency department. I'm passing this along to GI so they know before your visit on the 10th.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Follow-up and Colonoscopy
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY GROUP - CLINIC NOTE AND PROCEDURE SUMMARY
Visit and colonoscopy: 02/10/2025

Ms. Winslow is a 29-year-old we met last June for screening planning after childhood Wilms tumor treatment. She is back sooner than planned. For about three months she has had intermittent diarrhea, fatigue and low-grade temperatures, has lost 10 pounds (4.5 kg) without trying, and had a single episode of hematochezia. She has not traveled and has had no recent antibiotics. Stool culture through primary care was negative for pathogens.

Medications: no prescription medications; vitamin D3 2000 units daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: older sister with hypertension and irritable bowel syndrome.
Social: wine one to two glasses a month; no smoking.

Exam: T 37.3 C (99.2 F), HR 88, BP 102/60, RR 20, weight 58.5 kg. Abdomen diffusely tender without rebound, hyperactive bowel sounds. Perianal inspection normal. Rectal: normal sphincter tone, stool guaiac positive.

Colonoscopy (same day, moderate sedation): patchy inflammation with intervening normal mucosa (skip lesions).

Assessment: Crohn disease.

Plan:
1. Pre-biologic screening: TB and hepatitis B testing.
2. If screening is negative, start adalimumab 40 mg subcutaneously every 2 weeks; our biologics coordinator will handle the prior authorization and specialty pharmacy.
3. Avoid live vaccines once on therapy; inactivated vaccines encouraged.
4. Follow up in clinic after induction.

Copy to primary care.

documents.title: Outside Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: GI note from 2/10 received. Colonoscopy: skip lesions, Crohn disease. Adalimumab planned after TB/HBV screen. Problem list updated.

documents.title: Specialty Pharmacy Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Specialty pharmacy called asking whether we are the prescriber for her adalimumab pens. Told them no, prescriber is her GI. They are verifying insurance for first shipment and had our office listed as PCP only. No action needed from us.

documents.title: Started Injections
documents.author: patient

documents.title: Re: Started Injections
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad you're started. Nothing needed from me right now. GI manages the medication. At your physical in May we'll go over vaccines, since a few are recommended while you're on it.

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Turned 30 yesterday. Yearly exam, and first time I've seen her since the Crohn diagnosis.

GI course: colonoscopy 2/10 showed skip lesions -> Crohn disease. Adalimumab 40 mg q2wk since mid-March, prescribed by GI. Within about a month the diarrhea settled; now 1-2 formed stools a day, no blood, no fevers. Energy better. Has regained some weight (58.5 at GI, about 61 today). Stopped alcohol in February.

Meds reconciled: adalimumab 40 mg SC q2 weeks (GI), vitamin D3 2000 units daily. NKDA.

Exam: well. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, normal bowel sounds. Breasts without mass, skin or nipple change; no axillary nodes. No rash, no joint swelling.

A/P
1. Crohn disease on adalimumab - responding per her report. GI follows. CBC, CMP today. No live vaccines.
2. Immunizations on TNF inhibitor - PCV20 given today. Flu and COVID this fall.
3. BRCA2 - now 30: screening mammogram ordered for June, MRI stays in November so they alternate roughly every 6 months.
4. Hx Wilms/abdominopelvic RT - her colonoscopy this year counts for now; GI will set the interval going forward.
5. Solitary kidney - Cr, UA.
6. PHQ-2 1.
RTC 1 yr, sooner prn.

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual visit, April vacation week. Feels well. Bowels normal, no bleeding or night sweats. Saw GI in September: on adalimumab, told to continue; she didn't get a note to us and I don't have one. Still not drinking.

Family update: her older sister was diagnosed last year with breast cancer in both breasts, at 35. Erin is understandably shaken; it has made her more attentive to her own screening, not less. She asked what more she should be doing, and we went over the current plan (MRI and mammogram alternating) and that ovarian planning can be a separate visit when she wants it.

Meds: adalimumab 40 mg SC every 2 weeks (GI); vitamin D3 2000 units. NKDA.

Exam: well, weight up to 62 kg. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Breast exam: no dominant mass, no skin or nipple changes, axillae clear, both sides. Pelvic: normal, Pap/HPV collected. Skin clear. No joint findings.

A/P
1. Crohn disease - quiescent on adalimumab per her. Labs today. GI letter requested again.
2. BRCA2, strengthened family history - mammogram ordered for June; MRI November. Breast self-awareness reviewed.
3. Hx Wilms tumor, solitary kidney - Cr, UA.
4. Cervical screening - Pap with HPV today.
5. Lipids today (due).
6. PHQ-2 1. Support around sister's illness offered; she declined counseling referral for now.
RTC 1 yr.

documents.author: PCP

documents.title: Breast Surgery Consultation
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
OUTSIDE SURGICAL GROUP - BREAST SURGERY CONSULTATION
Date of service: 08/05/2026

31-year-old elementary school teacher, self-referred for a firm, nontender mass she noticed on self-examination of the left breast.

History: BRCA2 mutation carrier, followed with annual breast MRI and mammography. Crohn disease on adalimumab. Childhood Wilms tumor treated with left nephrectomy and abdominopelvic radiation at age 6, no recurrence.
Medications: adalimumab 40 mg SC every 2 weeks; vitamin D3 2000 units daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: older sister with bilateral breast cancer at 35; mother with breast cancer at 45; maternal aunt with ovarian cancer at 52; maternal grandmother with breast cancer at 68.
Social: never smoker; drank wine socially, one to two glasses a month, until her Crohn diagnosis and none since. Teaches elementary school.

Exam: Left breast, upper outer quadrant: 2.4 cm firm mass. No overlying skin changes. No nipple retraction.

Imaging: Diagnostic mammogram today demonstrates a suspicious irregular lesion corresponding to the palpable finding.

Plan: Core needle biopsy has been arranged; result pending.

Discussion: She is worried about her chances of further cancers and asked about genetic testing for herself and her family. We discussed that inherited mutations in DNA-repair genes such as BRCA2 raise lifetime risk of both breast and ovarian cancer, that they are passed on in an autosomal dominant pattern, and that not every carrier develops cancer. We will see her again with the pathology.
